To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the combination of T‐cells and PD‐L expression is useful in predicting response in HER2+ breast cancers.

PD‐L‐1 expression was positively correlated with CD8+ cells and CD163+ tumor‐associated macrophages in HER2+ breast cancers, and the combination of CD8+ cells with PD‐L‐I expression was useful in predicting the response of patients with HER2 positive breast cancer to anti-HER2 targeted therapy.

1) PD‐L1 is expressed by both immune cells and tumor cells in a large number of HER2+ breast cancers; 2) PD‐L+ cells and CD8+ cells coexist in the tumor microenvironment of a large portion of HER2+ cancers; and 3) PD‐L expression in tumor cells is inversely associated with response to neoadjuvant HER2 targeted therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of multiplex immunohistochemistry in the assessment of immune reactions and PD‐L expression in HER2‐positive breast cancer, and the association of these factors with response to anti‐ HER2 neoadjuvants therapy.
the evaluation of immune reaction and PD‐L expression using a multiplex immunohistochemical assay in HER2+ breast cancers.
the evaluation of the immune response and the PD‐L1 protein expression using multiplex immunohistochemistry in patients with HER‐2-positive breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PD‐L1 is not a reliable biomarker for the response to HER2-targeted therapy in patients with breast cancer.

PD‐L1 is a prognostic factor in patients with HER-2+ breast cancer and may be useful in the evaluation of immune reaction and the prediction of response to anti-HER-2 neoadjuvants in patients with HER‐2+ breast cancer.
a multiplex assay for the detection of PD‐L1 in immune and tumor cells, together with the assessment of CD8+ TILs, is useful for predicting the response to anti‐ HER2 neoadjuvent treatment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PD‐L1 is a potential predictive biomarker for anti‐HER2 therapies, especially in combination with TILs.
we have developed a multiplex immunohistochemical assay that can be used in a clinical setting to predict response to anti‐her2 targeted therapy in HER2+ breast cancers.

PD‐L1 and TILs are both prognostic and predictive factors in patients with HER 2+ breast cancer and their combination may provide a more accurate assessment of the prognosis and response to anti‐ HER 2 targeted therapy in these patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PD‐L1 is not an independent predictor of pCR, but it may be used to identify patients who will not benefit from anti‐PD‐1 treatment.
PD‐L1 is not a good marker for predicting response to anti-HER2 targeted therapy.

PD‐L1 is expressed in a significant proportion of HER2+ breast cancers and that the combination of PD‐L1 with CD8+ cells may be useful for predicting the response to anti‐PD‐L1 therapy in patients with breast cancer.
